body:
Closes #20

**PRD ID:** S1.5 · **Threat IDs:** T-D3

## Acceptance
- [x] Per device and per file, whole-file sends (a `want`, a `need` with no list, or a `need` covering more than half the pieces) are allowed at most 3 times in any 60 s. Requests over the limit are dropped and nothing is sent. `LIMITS.wholeSends`/`wholeWindow`. Unit: "at most 3 whole-file sends…", "the window slides…". Browser: 20 wants made A send the photo 2 times, and 20 needs listing every piece made A send the clip 2 times. B's own drags earlier in the same minute used the third send.
- [x] Requests for a few pieces (≤ half) are allowed at most once a second per device per file. `LIMITS.pieceGap`. Unit: "…at most once a second…", and 40 retries 1.5 s apart are never dropped.
- [x] Dropped requests don't count. Only requests that `allow()` accepts are recorded. Unit: "dropped requests do not count…" asks every second for a minute and is allowed again at 60 s.
- [x] Requests for a file this device doesn't have are dropped before they're counted. `want`: `files.get` runs before `asks.allow`. `need`: `src` runs before `askKind`/`asks.allow`.
- [x] Counters are bounded: `forget(dev)` runs when a device leaves the room, and there are at most `LIMITS.askRecords` (2000). Stale counters go first, then the oldest. Unit: "a device that leaves is forgotten", "the counters are capped in number", "stale counters are dropped before a live one is pushed out". All limits are named in `LIMITS` (Rule 3).

## Edge case
- A real transfer that loses pieces on the relay still finishes: every relay-run transfer passes, including the late guest and the silent-device step.
- Per device: a third device D that asked once got photo-0.jpg byte-identical (direct and relay).
- After 60 s the same device can ask again: unit test "after 60 s the same device can ask again". This isn't in the browser test, because it would add a minute.

## Red (before the fix)
`f05ceef` (tests plus a stub that allows everything):
```
npm run test:unit       ℹ pass 60  ℹ fail 12   (all AssertionError)
node tests/two-browser.mjs
FAIL 20 wants for one photo made A send it 20 times (at most 3)
FAIL 20 needs listing every piece made A send the file 20 times (at most 3)
PASS a third device asked once and still got photo-0.jpg byte-identical
```

## Tested
`npm test` after `85f104d`, exit 0:
```
ℹ pass 72  ℹ fail 0
PASS went direct
PASS send to a silent device gave up and told the sender (after 10.0 s)
PASS 20 wants for one photo made A send it 2 times (at most 3)
PASS 20 needs listing every piece made A send the file 2 times (at most 3)
PASS a third device asked once and still got photo-0.jpg byte-identical
PASS late guest downloaded photo-0.jpg from B byte-identical
PASS went relay (encrypted)
PASS send to a silent device gave up and told the sender (after 10.0 s)
PASS 20 wants for one photo made A send it 2 times (at most 3)
PASS 20 needs listing every piece made A send the file 2 times (at most 3)
PASS a third device asked once and still got photo-0.jpg byte-identical
PASS late guest downloaded photo-0.jpg from B byte-identical
```
74 PASS, 0 FAIL across both runs.

## Notes
- Beyond the ticket (Rule 1): a `need` whose list repeats a piece or names one past the end is dropped. Without this, `[0, 0, …]` would count as "a few pieces" but resend piece 0 up to 300 times a second. A real receiver never sends such a list.
- A `need` list without `cs` is counted at the largest piece size, which gives the fewest pieces. It can't pass for "a few pieces" when it isn't one. A real receiver always sends `cs` with a list.
- Thumbnails (`thumb:<pid>`) are limited the same way, as their own file.
- `want` and a whole-file `need` for the same file share one counter.
- Leaving clears only devices that were in the room. A device id never seen in presence isn't cleared by presence changes, so a stranger can't reset its counter by making the room re-sync (S1.6 is still open). Such ids are bounded by `askRecords`.
- The second `test:` commit changed the browser check from "exactly 3" to "at most 3", as the ticket says. B's own earlier drags count towards the limit.
title: fix: rate-limit resend requests per device (S1.5)
